implementation: Independent PyTorch scalar residual-gradient implementation; no upstream code/data bundled.
differences: Poisson example uses a manufactured sine variation instead of the paper polynomial bump.
Burgers uses existing soft boundary/initial constraints rather than the upstream hard output transform.
Same collocation points serve physical and gradient losses; Adam only, no inverse parameters or L-BFGS.
RAR scores the physical residual using the existing Margam sampler.
